paper.title: Bandit-Based Charging with Beamforming for Mobile Wireless-Powered IoT Systems

settings.name_in_paper: UMC problem with unknown stationary CSI (combinatorial bandit with submodular utility reward)
unmapped: Reward is a sum over N sensors of a known non-decreasing concave Lipschitz (constant B) utility of the sensor energy, which depends on the expected harvested powers of the selected base arms and the context (initial energies)
Super arm is N_s base arms (one policy per slot); base arms with the same policy in different slots share the same mean
Observing a policy at a location reveals the rewards of other code words at the same location (side observations)
Context X_t (initial sensor energies) observed at the start of each round
settings.definition_quote: In each charging round $t$, we select a combination of $N_s$ base arms from all the $K$ base arms. These selected base arms are combined to form a super arm $S_t\subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{K})$ and $|S_t|=N_s$, which serves as the charging policy for round $t$.

settings.name_in_paper: UMC problem with unknown non-stationary CSI (UMCB-SW setting)
unmapped: Reward is a sum over N sensors of a known non-decreasing concave Lipschitz (constant B) utility of the sensor energy
Super arm is N_s base arms (one policy per slot)
Context X_t (initial sensor energies) observed each round
settings.definition_quote: The total change of the mean is defined as $V_I:=  \sum_{t=t_1+1}^{t_2} \lVert \bf{p}_{t}-\bf{p}_{t-1} \rVert_{\infty}$ ... For simplicity, $D$ and $V$ are used to denote $D_{[1,T]}$ and $V_{[1,T]}$ respectively.

symbols.B_lip: Lipschitz/smoothness constant B of the utility function
symbols.n_pol: number of charging policies |Gamma| = |L| x M
symbols.N_s: number of slots per round (size of super arm); K = |Gamma| N_s
symbols.Delta_max: max over base arms of the largest positive alpha-gap of super arms containing the arm
symbols.Delta_min: min over base arms of the smallest positive alpha-gap of super arms containing the arm

conditions: utility function non-decreasing, non-negative, concave with Lipschitz constant B
alpha = 1/2 - 1/(2e) approximation ratio of the GUA oracle (assumes conditions of Theorem 2)
tuning: confidence radius rho = sqrt(3 ln t / (2 T_{j,t}))

source.label: theorem:UMCB_bound
source.quote: The expected regret for \ref{alg:UMCB} is $\mathbb{E}(R_1(T)) \le \frac{\pi^2}{3}NK \cdot \Delta_{max} + 2NB|\Gamma| + \sum_{j\in [|L|]}\frac{48B^2NN_s \ln{T}}{\Delta_{min}}$, where $\Delta_{max}=\max_{a_k\in \mathcal{K}}\Delta^{a_k}_{max}$, $\Delta_{min}=\min_{a_k\in \mathcal{K}}\Delta^{a_k}_{min}$, and $B$ is constant to describe the smoothness of $U(q_i)$

results.notes: Regret R_1(T) = alpha*sum r_{S*_t} - sum r_{S_t} with alpha=1/2-1/(2e), recorded as alpha_regret. The sum over j in [|L|] of a constant gives |L| times the term. Gap definitions are super-arm based (paper's definition of Delta_min uses min(0,...), apparently a typo). Proof is informal. Theorems 1-2 (offline discretization / GUA approximation ratios) not recorded as bandit guarantees.

symbols.B_lip: Lipschitz/smoothness constant B of the utility function

conditions: utility function non-decreasing, concave with Lipschitz constant B
V is the total variation sum_t ||p_t - p_{t-1}||_inf over [1,T]

source.label: theorem:UMCBSW_bound
source.quote: Given $V$, the expected regret $\mathbb{E}(R_1(T)) \le \frac{\pi^2}{3}NK\cdot \Delta_{max} +(3-\frac{1}{e})KNB\sqrt{VT}  +2NB\sum_{l\in[|L|]} (\sqrt{VT}+1) (\sqrt{6\ln{T}} + \frac{24BN_s \ln{T}}{\Delta_{min}})$ when choosing $w=\min \{\sqrt{\frac{T}{V}},T\}$.

results.notes: Regret against alpha times the per-round optimum in a drifting environment. Learner needs V to set the window. Sum over l in [|L|] gives factor |L|.
